title: Host Gifts
short: A small host gift such as flowers in a vase, a treat or something for the pantry is welcome; it is for the host to enjoy later, not to serve that night.
trouble: Learners expect the host to open and serve what they brought, or bring cut flowers that pull the host away to find a vase. Customs on host gifts vary by region.

blocks.html: When you arrive at someone's home for a meal or party, a small gift is a way of saying thank you before the evening even starts.
A small host gift is welcome: flowers already in a vase, a treat, something for the pantry. It is for the host to enjoy later, not to serve that night.

A host has planned the menu and the evening. A gift that must be used right away, such as a dish to serve or loose flowers that need a vase, pulls the host away from guests and into the kitchen, which is the opposite of a thank-you. A gift to enjoy later gives pleasure without adding work.

cards.text: Flowers already arranged in a vase

cards.why: The host must stop and find a vase.

cards.text: A dish you expect the host to serve tonight
cards.why: It upsets the host's menu. Bring a dish only when asked.

cards.text: A jar of good jam for breakfast

blocks.title: The gift at the door
blocks.q: James hands Priya a box of chocolates at the door. She thanks him and sets it on a side table. Should she open it for dessert?
steps: A host gift is for the host to enjoy later.
Priya may share it if she likes, but she doesn't have to.
James should not expect to see it served.
blocks.a: No need: it is hers to enjoy later.

blocks.title: Flowers for the host
blocks.q: Ruby wants to bring flowers to a dinner. How can she make them easy for the host?
steps: Loose flowers mean a search for a vase in the middle of greeting guests.
She brings flowers already arranged in a vase, or a potted plant, or has flowers delivered before or after.
blocks.a: Bring them already in a vase, or send them another day.

blocks.html: Expecting the host to open and serve what you brought, or bringing cut flowers that pull the host away to find a vase. A host gift says thank you; it should never add work. Customs on host gifts vary by region.

Customs differ: in some regions and families a host gift is expected; in others it is a pleasant extra. In some countries certain flowers or numbers of flowers carry special meanings. Ask someone who knows the custom.
